files.changed: Only the workspace parts are kept: the members are the 4 ported crates in crates/ and the new sqll binary crate (crates/sqll), the workspace dependencies that they use, and the release profile. The workspace version is the sqll version. New: serde_json and sha2 (for build.rs of sqll_dialects), and opt-level 3 for sha2; regex-syntax (S3 T15, the match prefixes of the lexer regexes in sqll_types matcher.rs), the version that regex uses. No root package, no feature "python", no pyo3. S3 T17 (parse speed, build profile): the release profile has lto = "fat" and codegen-units = 1, so that the parser inlines the accessors of sqll_types; about 10% fewer instructions in the parse. S3 T18: the members also have the rules crate (crates/sqll_rules) and the native tests of the root crate (crates/sqll_base_tests). S3b C6: the members also have the syntax tree crate (crates/sqll_tree) and the interface test crate (crates/sqll_interfaces). S3b C7: the members also have the syntax crate (crates/sqll_syntax).

S3 T18: Arena::from_node is public (pub, not pub(crate)), so that the rules crate (sqll_rules) and its tests can make an arena from a parse tree. The source makes it only in the Python bindings (python.rs, not ported). The parse does not use it.

Parser has the field limit_error: the first parser limit error (iterations, depth, or nodes) of the parse. check_parse_subtree_limit records its error there, and root_parse and call_rule_as_root clear it at the start. Parser has the field current_depth: the parse depth of the frame that the innermost parse loop processes. See the reason of iterative.rs. S3 T16 (parse speed, copy): each parse frame is in a box (TableParseFrame is Box<TableParseFrameData>), so that the stack and the handlers move a pointer, not the 312 bytes of the frame; new_child gives the box. The parse does not change. S3 T16 (parse speed, memo): MatchResult has a memo of node_count (NodeCountMemo; T17 renamed it MatchMemo), so that the node limit check of each completed frame does not count each subtree again; Debug prints the 4 match fields as before. The parse does not change. S3 T16 (parse speed, allocation): StringParser and TypedParser read the type id lists from the tables only on a match. S3 T17 (parse speed, memo): the memo field of MatchResult has the new name memo. S3 T17 (parse speed, regex): handle_regex_parser reads the aux data with no copy of a string, the regex cache key is the pattern id (not the pattern text, which can be a long keyword list), and the anti-pattern is tried (and compiled) only after the pattern matches. A match needs the pattern and not the anti-pattern, as before. The parse does not change. S3 T17 (parse speed, copy): MatchResult.matched_class is Option<Box<MatchedClass>>, so that a match result is 88 bytes, not 296, to move and copy; each construction puts the class in a box.
Only a comment: the doc comment of terminator_matches_at says that a parser limit error stops the parse through Parser.limit_error (core.rs). See the reason of iterative.rs.

S3 T16 (parse speed, memo): MatchResult has a memo of node_count (NodeCountMemo; T17 renamed it MatchMemo), so that the node limit check of each completed frame does not count each subtree again; Debug prints the 4 match fields as before. The parse does not change. S3 T16 (parse speed, allocation): apply puts the metas and the child matches in a list sorted by position (the same order), not in a hash map of lists, and moves the child matches out of the match result, so that a child that is not shared is not copied. S3 T17 (parse speed, memo): the memo of a match result (MatchMemo, field memo) also keeps the result of contains_unparsable, so that OneOf does not scan each candidate subtree again for each comparison. The parse does not change. S3 T17 (parse speed, copy): MatchResult.matched_class is Option<Box<MatchedClass>>, so that a match result is 88 bytes, not 296, to move and copy; each construction puts the class in a box. S3b C8 (the source map): apply retags a single token match only if the token gives a raw node. The source took the node out of the list before it checked that it was a raw node, so the root match of a file with only the end_of_file token (the empty templated text that the Jinja templater gives, with no slices) gave a file node with no children. sqlfluff gives the file with its end_of_file segment. The record of the source map (results/S3b/C8-source-map.json, the empty dialect fixture) checks it. The raw templater gives a placeholder and end_of_file for an empty file, so the output of sqll parse does not change.

Above the iteration limit (rust_parser_max_iterations), the parser returns a ParseError, not a panic. Each sub-parse (the main parse and each probe) has its own count of iterations. A probe sub-parse starts at the parse depth of the frame that starts it (Parser.current_depth, core.rs), so max_parse_depth also limits nesting through probes (for example bracketed joins), and thus the native stack. In the source, each probe starts at depth 0, and about 36000 nested bracketed joins (612 KB) overflow the stack of the sqll command thread (256 MiB). Each parse loop stops with the first parser limit error (iterations, depth, or nodes) of the parse (Parser.limit_error, core.rs), because a probe for a terminator or a delimiter drops its error and counts it as no match. The diagnostic text (cache statistics and the tokens near the position) is only in the feature "verbose-debug", and the token lines go to stderr. That feature does not build: a borrow error in core.rs (about line 1566) that is also in the source. Thus "sqll parse" gives a parse error with exit code 1, and stdout has only the JSON record. sqlfluff with the Rust parser stops with a PanicException and exit code 1. S3 T16 (parse speed, copy): each parse frame is in a box (TableParseFrame is Box<TableParseFrameData>), so that the stack and the handlers move a pointer, not the 312 bytes of the frame; new_child gives the box. The parse does not change.

S3 T17 (parse speed, terminator checks): greedy_match does not probe a terminator at a position where its simple hint matches no token from that position to the first code token (terminator_hint_excludes); the result is false, as the probe gives if it does not reach a parser limit. Python's next_match also tries only the matchers that the simple hints allow. The check scripts/s3/hint_check.py (results/s3/speed/T17-hint-check.json) also runs each excluded probe on the 2306 dialect fixtures and the 84 S2 parse inputs: 974128 exclusions, no probe match, no probe at a parser limit, and the same output. Thus the trees do not change on these 2390 inputs. A probe that is not run cannot reach a parser limit (depth, iterations, or nodes). Thus on such an input sqll can give a tree where the source stops the parse (harness/sqll.md); the sqlfluff Python parser also does not run these probes.

S3 T15 (parse speed, the fixed cost of each run): a lexer regex compiles at its first use, not when the dialect makes its matchers (LexerMode::Lazy and LazyRegex; the clones of a matcher share the compiled regex). The compile is that of the source: the regex crate, then fancy_regex, then the fallback function. Before the compile, scan_match also checks the match prefixes of the pattern (match_prefixes: the literal extraction of regex_syntax); if the input does not start with one of them, no match can start there, so the regex does not compile and the result is None, as in the source. A pattern with a fallback function compiles before the precheck, because the source does not apply the precheck to the function. A pattern that does not compile and has no fallback panics at its first use, not when the matchers are made (a test compiles each pattern of each dialect).

S3b C8 (the source map): the newline index of the source text and of the templated text has code point offsets, as the sqlfluff Python TemplatedFile (iter_indices_of_newlines, str.find). The source used byte offsets (char_indices), so get_line_pos_of_char_pos, which takes a code point offset, gave a wrong line position after a multi-byte character (S3b C7 finding). A new unit test checks it. For the 2306 dialect fixtures and the 84 S2 parse inputs, the output of sqll parse does not change. S3b C8 also: templated_slice_to_source_slice takes no start slice when the insertion point moves the start index after the stop index, as the Python slice gives []. The source panicked (an index range that starts after its end) for a file with source slices out of order, where sqlfluff gives a source slice. The start slices are not used in that case (the insertion point is the start), so each other answer does not change. A new unit test in this file and the unit tests of crates/sqll_source/src/map.rs check it. S3b C8 also: raw_slices_spanning_source_slice adds the code point length of the last raw slice (chars().count()), as the Python len, to its code point offset (source_idx). The source added the byte length, so after a multi-byte character a source slice at the end of the file gave a raw slice, where sqlfluff gives none. A new unit test checks it with the answers of sqlfluff.
